Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National No new taxes in 2027 will bring relief to Ghanaians – Taxpayers League Source : Albert Kuzor 16 November 2026 11:43am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Taxpayers League Ghana has commended the government for its decision not to introduce new taxes in the 2027 Budget, saying the move could ease financial pressures on households and businesses.
The organisation described the decision as a welcome development at a time when Ghanaians are seeking economic relief, improved purchasing power and a more favourable business environment.
In a press release signed by its Executive Director, Hopeson Adorye, on November 15, the League said taxation should not be viewed merely as a tool for generating revenue but should also serve as a means of promoting investment, stimulating production, protecting jobs and supporting economic growth.
It said the government's decision, announced by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, signals a commitment to improving revenue mobilisation through stronger tax compliance, plugging revenue leakages and ensuring the effective collection of existing taxes.
Taxpayers League Ghana also welcomed the government's earlier removal of several taxes, including the Electronic Transfer Levy (E-Levy), COVID-19 Levy, Emissions Levy, withholding tax on betting and lottery winnings, and VAT on motor vehicle insurance.
According to the organisation, these measures provide an opportunity to rebuild public confidence in the tax system and strengthen the relationship between the government and taxpayers.
However, it stressed that the absence of new taxes must translate into tangible economic benefits for ordinary Ghanaians.
The League called for greater accountability and transparency in the management of public funds, intensified efforts to eliminate corruption and waste, and simpler tax administration to make compliance less burdensome for individuals and businesses.
It also urged the government to prioritise job creation, infrastructure development and investment in productive sectors to ensure that economic stability leads to improved living conditions.
The organisation further called on the government to maintain its no-new-tax commitment throughout 2027.
“Ghana does not necessarily need more taxes to generate more revenue; it needs a more efficient, transparent and accountable revenue collection system,” the statement said.
